Subject: Regional hosting guarantees & VPC segmentation questions

Hi Rishi + team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of our SIG/SOC2 intake we need a concise confirmation of two things so we can close out our security questionnaire:

1) Region enforcement: we need a short statement describing how Redwood ensures customer workloads for Medicore are physically served only from EU-only nodes (we'll be looking for the specific host naming or region tags you can provide as evidence).

2) VPC/private deployment controls: we need a VPC segregation matrix showing what is shared vs tenant-dedicated (network paths, bastion/jumpbox access, operator/admin consoles, and any cross-tenant egress paths).

If possible please include pointers to: SOC2 control IDs (or exhibits) that map to these controls, a minimal CAIQ/SIG reference (we don't need the whole questionnaire, just the relevant rows), and any short-runbook or ops playbook that outlines how you respond to region/fencing incidents.

We're on a tight timeline — would you be able to send an initial packet by EOD Monday (Apr 14)? If you have a signed letter or a one-page region guarantee we can circulate to our legal/compliance team that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Baker
Security Program Manager | Medicore Health
security@medicore.com

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely provide the artifacts you outlined. Quick clarifying Qs so we scope precisely:

• When you say “EU-only nodes” do you need a run of live hostnames (we can provide a hostmap snapshot) or would a signed hosting commitment plus host naming convention plus ephemeral audit logs suffice?
• For the VPC segregation matrix: do you want the logical view (services and whether they are shared) or the physical network diagram with subnets/bastion flow? We can provide both; the latter will include a short bastion access policy.

Plan: Marissa will produce the VPC segregation spreadsheet and an ops runbook extract. I’ll draft a one-page hosting commitment letter that we can sign (and put in DocuSign if Medicore prefers). Irene will map the relevant SIG/CAIQ rows to our existing SOC2 exhibits.

Target: initial packet with the spreadsheet and the hosting letter by Monday EOD as requested. If you need anything sooner let me know and we’ll prioritize.

—Rishi

Hi Alice — adding the technical detail you'll likely want.

Summary (short):
• Tenant network isolation: customer compute runs in tenant-scoped pools (tenant IDs are mapped to dedicated vGPU pools in EU regions). Control plane (control plane APIs, management) is logically separated and requires RBAC + audited operator sessions.
• Bastion/jumpbox access: operator access to tenant pools is via ephemeral bastion instances; sessions are audited and require MFA + just-in-time approval.
• Egress: default egress is blocked; any outbound endpoints (e.g., to updates/metrics) use pinned egress proxies in EU zones and require allowlist approvals.

I'm attaching the segmentation matrix (tabbed by service) and a short extract of the runbook that shows the incident checklist for region-breaks and forced workload rebind. The hostmap snapshot we plan to provide will include timestamped hostnames with region tags (e.g., eu-west-1-node-<id>), and we can produce a filtered snapshot that only shows accounts and hosts serving Medicore.

Deliverables (what you'll see Monday):
1) segregation matrix (XLSX) — what is shared vs dedicated by service + fields to show network paths and operator access.
2) runbook excerpt (PDF) — incident play for region/fencing; includes contact roles.
3) hostmap snapshot (TXT) — filtered list tied to date/time for audit.

If Medicore needs a live walkthrough of the hostmap export format before you accept it as evidence, happy to set a 30-min session.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Security Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Thanks — this is exactly the right structure. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

• Evidence format: Our audit team prefers an authoritative artifact rather than a CSV — examples: a timestamped hostmap snapshot exported from your inventory system (sha256 sum would be great), or a signed PDF letter referencing the hostnames and the timestamp.
• SIG/CAIQ mapping: can Irene provide the SIG rows but also enumerate which SOC2 exhibits correspond to those rows? A quick 1:1 mapping (SIG row -> SOC2 exhibit ID) is what our assessor needs.
• DocuSign: if you can send the one-page hosting commitment via DocuSign that would speed legal review.

If you can provide the hostmap snapshot with a sha256 and the DocuSign link by Monday EOD we're good to start the assessment. If there are any items that are likely to take longer, can you flag them now?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — HS-4521 is tracking this intake.
